There are other examples, too, of Zoran's help and co-operation and asking people whether he could do anything to help. And the man I just mentioned, Mr. Senad Topoljak, he also lived in Vitez. He had his apartment awarded to him by the factory where he lived with his sister. He was from the village of Lupac. His sister worked in a store. So in the chaos that ensued, that young man really didn't really know what to do. So together Zoran and I went to Senad's apartment and we took what we could to him. From Caritas we would take flour to the apartment. We would visit him. And we were in touch with him all the time, for as long as Senad was in Vitez. Zoran was more in touch with him than I was, because I had to go for bandaging. So I know that on one occasion I was coming back from getting new bandages and Zoran said, "Well, I don't feel comfortable going by myself. But if you come with me, would you please come so I could see if Majda Sivro was still in the apartment."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Majda Sivro"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Majda Sivro, yes, she's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that after the crime in Ahmici Zoran did not go back to Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No. Zoran never went back to his family house there and he said that after all that had happened there, he didn't have the will, simply, to live there any more. He stayed in Vitez with his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His house is empty? It's been empty since then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know Mirjan Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I met Mirjan through Zoran maybe in 1988, 1989, and then in '91, '92, already in '91, we would meet because Zoran would usually -- we would go from work, after 2.00, two or three times a week for a drink and for a game of billiards. Since Zoran was in the cultural society, they had their own premises in the building, and there was also a room there where there was a cafe where they had a billiards table and where members of the cultural society would gather. And he felt the most comfortable there probably, so he would often take Senad and me there. He would suggest that we go there for a drink and play a game or two of billiards. That's where, on one occasion, I met Mr. Mirjan Kupreskic, and he said -- well, I knew at that time they were both Kupreskics, but I didn't know they were brothers. So that's when I met Mirjan and many other members of the cultural society, and when they would go there more frequently, I would join them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how did Mirjan behave? What kind of positions did he voice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Mirjan's stand in all of that was similar to the one that Zoran had. It could be said that they had the same positions in many circumstances. They had the same view of life. As far as the opinion about the war, we all shared similar opinions, but for them, music was important, their jobs, their family. They tried to stay apart from everything, and I think they succeeded in doing so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that they were socialising with Fahran Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Fahran Ahmic, Fahrudin, a Muslim, he was my colleague from work. We were foremen at a job, and that's where we met. And then later when I would go to the cultural society offices with Fahran, then I noticed that they were much better friends with Fahran, that they knew each other through this music, and they seemed to be extremely good friends, and we went together to Fahran's house. We would meet up at Zoran's house, Fahran's, Senad Topoljak's, so it all functioned in the best possible way then. They didn't make any difference -- they didn't differentiate between their friends in the cultural society or outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end, could you please tell the Court, since you had such good relations with Zoran Kupreskic, would Zoran Kupreskic tell you if he had known anything about the attack that was being prepared on the 16th of April? If he had known something, would he have told you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: In any case, I'm convinced that he would tell me. Not only Zoran, and I was exceptional friends with him, but many people who lived there or in other places, even people that I wasn't as friendly with as I was with Zoran, if anybody -- especially Zoran, if he had known anything, he would have either called me in the evening or in the morning, and he would have advised me to take shelter. We talked by telephone often, so I'm sure he would have told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. President, I have no further questions, and I would just like D52/2 and D60/2 to be submitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: D59, okay, and D60. Yes, D59 and D60. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. They are admitted into evidence. Is there any cross-examination by other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have two questions for the witness, and the other Defence counsel will not examine this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Pavkovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, I'm counsel Petar Pavkovic. You mentioned on a couple of occasions Kuber. What is that, in fact, Kuber? What is this about? Could you please clarify this for us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned Kuber because Kuber was a dominant point, an elevation as regards Poculica, Vrhovine, and Prnjavor. So in '92 when the village guards were formed, we would contact all the villages in between because behind Kuber, towards Zenica, there were one or two larger villages that were populated by Serbs. And also the road from Kuber led to Busovaca where there was Kratine with some Serbs there as well. So there were suspicions that supplies and weapons were being transferred from there so that we, the three or four villages, concluded that it would be good to go up there for five days at a time with five or six men to keep watch, and this is what we did. But I was in charge to maintain contacts with our neighbours, Muslims, who didn't keep watch at that time to make it possible for us, to give us passage, so that we would just go up there, five, six, ten men, and this is how we did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from a military standpoint, this was an important elevation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall any of those people who went there to keep watch in this period that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I can, of course, remember. There were people from Gornja Dubravica, people from Marosa. So these men would come and then we would change shifts. There were boys from Zume, from Santici, Vidovici, Livancici, and Drebci, these were their last names. I knew some of these men at that time and before, and then some of them I got to know. I remember their faces, their names. It was mostly Vidovici, Drebci, Livancici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name Zeljo Livancic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Zeljo would change shifts with us. Zeljo's group would replace my group, so I knew him very well. He took part in the agreements together with us. He was a representative of the Croats. He and four other people were there. So we thought these were the people who would do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Zeljo Livancic, is he alive today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: According to my information or according to what I heard, Zeljo was killed at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps find out from those talks when he was killed, roughly, if you can tell us the time? It seems that the 16th is a date that most events are remembered by.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Well, according to some information, this happened immediately on the 16th. According to some, it happened a day after that on the 17th, but I know that Busovaca also had a strategic point, so that on the evening of the 15th, some one or two men were already killed there, one or two Croats. I can't tell you exactly whether this was the 15th, the 16th, or the 17th, but I know he was killed at Kuber, and then five days before, as I said, my group from Poculica was there, I wasn't in that group, and they came back. And then later Zeljo, with his group, came to replace them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Pavkovic. I think we can now move on to the cross-examination by the Prosecution. Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Bill Smith, and I appear for the Prosecution with Mr. Terrier and Mr. Blaxill. With your leave. Cross-examined by Mr. Smith:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, thank you very much for your testimony. I work for the Prosecution. It's my job to ask you some specific questions about what you've said in court today just to clarify some issues. Firstly, I'd like you to look at a map which I'll produce to you, and I'll ask you some questions about particular locations on that map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 345.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a segment of an earlier exhibit that the Prosecution has tendered already. It just focuses in on the Vitez and Poculica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, does that map look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I'm just trying to see. I haven't seen it before, but I know the layout of these villages and the settlements which are shown on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can get you to mark with the pen the village of Poculica, if you can just place an underline on the map.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I could but it's written wrong. Where it says "Poculica" here is, in fact, where the village of Prnjavor is. I will mark here where Poculica is. It's not where it's shown to be. (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a figure number 1 next to that? Can you write the numeral 1 next to that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Okay. (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village where Poculica appears on the map, that is Prnjavor, is that correct, where the word "Poculica" appears?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prnjavor is completely a Muslim settlement, is that correct, people of Muslim origin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the same for Vrhovine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stated in your evidence that the local community of Poculica covered those three particular villages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated in your evidence that Tolovici was initially a Serb village but they evacuated prior to April '93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vjetrenica was a Muslim village, exclusively Muslim village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Vjetrenica itself was -- the top of the village was purely Muslim, but then as it went down towards Vitez, it was mixed. There were Croats and Muslims. So in its upper part, it was purely Muslim, but then about 200 metres further down, it was mixed, and then as it went further along, there were only Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Poculica itself, the specific village of Poculica, Muslims lived at the upper part of the village and Croats lived at the lower part of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, and then in my earlier testimony, I divided the village into three parts. So the lower part was purely Croatian, the central part was 60 per cent Croats, 40 per cent Muslims, and then the upper part of the village of Poculica was maybe 50/50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also on that map, do you see the Kuber range, the Kuber mountain range? It's difficult to read but I think you should see it there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I'm trying to see. Kuber should be above Vrhovine towards the right. Yes, Saracevica, Jelinak, Loncari, Kratina. I'm sorry. I can't find Kuber. I know roughly where it's supposed to be, but it's not written down here, so I can't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is very difficult to read. It is, actually, written on the map, but in any event --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Where is it on the map, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you look at Vrhovine, and just to the right, it runs at 45 degrees.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Okay. I know where it is, but I thought that you wanted me to read to you where it is. That's what I thought you wanted but I, of course, know where it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Poculica is only a kilometre or so away from the Kuber mountain range; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, no, that's not right. I've said that, as the crow flies, we were maybe 700 metres away. So maybe as the crow flies, it's less than a kilometre, but if you walk, then it's about two and a half kilometres away from Poculica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Croat population within Poculica was largely surrounded by a Muslim pocket of villages; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to show you a photograph, a copy of an aerial photograph, which is a segment of Prosecution Exhibit P1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 346.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, you see that that photograph largely covers the area of Poculica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Poculica, Prnjavor, and Vrhovine, so that's the complete local community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the lower part of Poculica, could you put a mark on that map where the actual village begins with a numeral 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: The village begins here (indicating). At the beginning of the photograph, that's where the beginning of the village is. This road to the left that you can see, that's the road to Sljivcica. It's a pebble road, and it led to Mahala, but it's very hard to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, could the witness place the map on the ELMO so that we could also follow what he is marking on the map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: This is the beginning of the village (indicating) from the beginning of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's where the Croat houses commenced; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map, with a line just going across the main road, the Vitez-Zenica road, where the purely Croat houses finish before we get to the next area? Perhaps if you can mark it with a pen and then place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many Croat houses are in that purely Croat area of the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure exactly how many. Just give me a moment so I can figure it out in my head. Up to about 40 houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were the houses that were destroyed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, the houses that were destroyed, but not all of them were destroyed. Where I placed the mark, that's where the last Muslim house is, and then below that last Muslim house, there were ten houses which were Croat houses, but they were untouched, and they have now been settled by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the next part of the village along the road as we go towards Zenica, is that a mixed part where Croats were living and Muslims were living; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. That ratio I mentioned, there were a little more Croats there. The ratio was 60 to 40, and then down here, further down, I can mark that for you where it was half and half. That's this part here. (Marks).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's just before the bend in the road as you go up towards Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any specific point in the village? You mentioned a school and a mosque. Does that point correspond with the school or the mosque or any other particular significant feature?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand. The mosque corresponds to the mosque, it has a minaret, and the school is where you go to school. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my fault. Can you place on the map where the mosque is in Poculica, please, and if you could mark in pen with the letter "M"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it. I'll point it out. The felt pen is red so you can see it (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where the pointer is is where the mosque is. You also mentioned in your testimony a school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Can I indicate it? (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate it again with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area that you've marked as the mixed part of the village where it was 60 per cent Croat and 40 per cent Muslim, from the end point that you've put on that map towards Zenica, is it purely Muslim from there on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No. You mean this part of the last line I drew?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, no. This is not purely Muslim. I said that the part on from there was 50/50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a road. The road seems to turn off towards Prnjavor, and the main road continues on to Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the road that turns off to Prnjavor, can you mark on the map where the purely Muslim section starts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can't be very accurate, but I can mark this road where I placed the mosque. So you can see here from the main road, there is a road, a macadam road turning off the main road, and that used to be the road to Zenica. But afterwards when the asphalt road was built, this side road remained as this macadam road, and on the right-hand side towards the village, there were purely Muslim houses. And beneath the mosque on the left-hand side and around the mosque, there were Croat houses too, the Jurcevic, Papic, Kristo families. Behind the mosque, let me think, about 150 to 200 metres away was the border of the village of Poculica, and then came the purely Muslim village of Prnjavor. I'm going to show it to you right now. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that spot that you indicated with the pointer, that is where the purely Muslim village commences; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area that you stated there was about a 60/40 Croat-Muslim mix, in that particular area of Poculica were there any houses damaged in that area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, two houses were torched. I marked the school here for you, and about 15 metres away from the school, roughly, on this side of the road, Mr. Ramljak's house, Mr. Stipo Ramljak's house was burnt down. Actually, two of his houses were burnt down. He was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once we move into the part of the village above the mosque, where you stated that it was 50/50 Muslim and Croat, were there any houses destroyed or burnt down as a result of the attack on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. We couldn't have burned it. We couldn't have reached the upper part of the village, let alone Prnjavor. Later in the afternoon, I don't know, I have no idea. From our side, not a single Muslim house was destroyed or burnt, either in Prnjavor or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in terms of damage that occurred as a result of the conflict on the 16th and after the 16th of April, 1993, the main damage that occurred in Poculica was in the lower part of the village where about 40 or 41 houses were damaged, some very badly damaged and destroyed, and some not so badly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, that's not right. I said that there were Croat houses in Poculica, in the local community, forty-two that were destroyed. And not all of them are in this lower part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (Microphone not on)

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, yes, in the lower part and even in this upper part. I am going to put some kind of a sign here for you to see. X, for instance. This sign here, this is where the macadam Road forks off leading to our cemetery, Zvizda, and also the Papic, Tomic and other family houses, these were Croat houses, 20 or 25 of them, and they were totally destroyed as well. And these houses, together with the houses in the lower part of the village, make up a total of 42. So they are on this side and that side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you place on the map where your house is. I was wondering -- (no microphone). Can you mark your house, the general area with a "DG.".

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I didn't understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you find the general location of your house and mark it with the initials "DG," please. Can you also indicate that with a pointer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I can. Just a minute. Let me find it. Here. Here (indicating), exactly here where this road turns off. This is also macadam Road that people used when they were walking on foot or when they were going by cart, and this is where my house is. When you get off this road here. Here, right over here (indicating). There was a monument here dedicated to the partisan days here. Here. This is where my house is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned that Mara Papic, you went to Mara Papic's house. Could you place on the map the location of where her house is with "MP," please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Mara Papic, her house is here. Let me just find it -- here (indicating). Right over here. The last house bordering on the last Muslim house. That's where the border line is. And right next to the border line is Mara Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the distance from her house to your house is about (no microphone)? You give the figure. How far away is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Could you please try to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far away from your house is Mara Papic's house, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: About 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. In relation to this map, I think largely that's been dealt with, so perhaps it's a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can just concentrate on the 15th of April and what happened that day before the shelling on the 16th. I think you said that you went to Vitez on the afternoon of the 15th, then you came back about 4.30 or 5.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. I set out for Vitez around noon, perhaps around 12.00, I don't know exactly, and I spent about three or four hours there, so possibly that was the time when I came back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came back and you said that the atmosphere in the village was a little bit tense because of the killings of some bodyguards in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. The bodyguards, escorts of the commander of the Zenica brigade, Zivko Totic, were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the only thing that in your mind seemed to make things tense in that particular village, that incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, that day was that incident. And also before that it was a bit tense and it wasn't all the same to us, all these other incidents that had occurred before that. An HVO officer killed in Travnik and then the incidents in Novi Travnik, Ahmici, Busovaca, Dusina, all sorts of things were going on. It was always tense. That day too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, in any event, you decided to walk around the village to see that everything was okay, and with the Croats and the Muslims and, as far as you were concerned, things were okay, despite the fact that there was this fear in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to bed that night? You weren't on guard on the night of the 15th, were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first thing that you heard of anything unusual was when two guards woke you up about 5.00 in the morning, and they had mentioned that some lady may have said that there might be an attack either in the village or in the area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, as a result of that, you went to Mara Papic's house that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then she told you that her sister had rung from, I think it was Krtina Mahala, and said that there was shooting in that particular area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That is not correct. I did not say that she ran there. I said that her sister from Krtina Mahala had phoned, so she had phoned Mara Papic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, that was my mispronunciation. I meant that her sister had rung her. At the time that you spoke to Mara Papic, could you hear shooting in distant villages or in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Probably I could have had there been any shooting, but at that time there wasn't any shooting, so I couldn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any shooting coming from the Ahmici area, Ahmici-Santici area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, later, when I set out for the lower part of the village from that area, Santici, Ahmici, Vitez, down from that area, yes, I could hear shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of what Mara Papic had said to you, you decided to ring your friend Mario Cerkez at the Viteska Brigade command headquarters in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That is not correct. I talked to the person on duty in headquarters and he told me that Mario was not there and that he would try to find Mario. And if he would somehow get in touch with Mario, that he would ask him to call me back, to try to call me back at Mara Papic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You intended to ring Mario Cerkez, though, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mario Cerkez rang you back some minutes later?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps some 10 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated to him that you felt there seemed to be some fear in the village, because information was coming in from other villages that there might be an attack. That's what you told Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he said to you, "Did you notice anything unusual in the village?" And you told him that you didn't. And, I think you said in your evidence, that Mario recommended that you continue your observation in the particular village and that you would talk later with Mario Cerkez, if it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then that's when the conversation ended?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that time you were of the view that if something significant occurred in the village, you would have rung Mario Cerkez and informed him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I knew Mario Cerkez from the factory and we worked together. And, as I knew that he was in the headquarters there, that he was down there, I had no one else to talk to. Yes, I asked to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the phone call, you said at some time later you heard some shooting from the village of Ahmici and Santici, villages of Ahmici and Santici. About how long after that phone call did you hear that shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps after some 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that could have been about 5.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes. Yes. Something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear shelling coming from that direction as well? Sorry, did you hear shelling noises in that direction, the direction of Ahmici and Santici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, then at that time I couldn't exactly tell. Shooting could be heard, but then we were so frightened, so it was difficult to tell the exact location. It seemed at first that the shooting was coming from the town of Vitez itself, and later on it also came from the direction of Santici, Ahmici, all of it was mixed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the commander of the village guard in Poculica, the HVO commander of the village guard in Poculica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That is not correct. I was one of the representatives of the Croat people in all these negotiations, and there were five of us on this crisis staff. We were not organised as an army at all, and I was no commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll use a different term. You were the coordinator of the Croat village guard in Poculica. You coordinated the guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a deputy coordinator?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I said that there were a few of them, Zoran Jurcevic -- I'm sorry. It wasn't Jurcevic. It was Marijan Grbavac, Tomislav Gruban ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were coordinators as such. They assisted you in the coordination. About how many Croats did you have in the village guard in Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: At the beginning, there were five or six Croats in the village guards in Poculica with at least one or two hunting guns. And as time went by, as the situation changed, as there were more and more incidents, the village guard was enlarged too. In a normal situation, it could have been up to 30 or 40 men who joined up because, at that time, there was looting, and people were ashamed to be asleep while we were patrolling the village. So later they came to join the village guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just referring to April '93, about how many men did you have in the village guard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, perhaps around 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a number of them that were in the active Viteska Brigade as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, no, those who were in the village guard were not in the active component.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tomislav Jursevic, he was in the active brigade, the Viteska Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't know a person called Tomislav Josevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have difficulty pronouncing these names, so if I can spell it. It's J-U-R-C-E-V-I-C.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. When this active component was established, yes, Tomislav Jurcevic was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was in the Viteska Brigade before April 1993, wasn't he, or are you not sure?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, I know that before April, this active component or whatever was established. I don't know exactly when in 1993 and I don't know how many men there were there exactly, but I do know that the people who were in this active component said that they would not join the village guard anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Mario Cerkez spoke to you when you rang him about what Mara Papic had said, he didn't tell you that there was going to be a Bosnian army attack coming from the direction of Kuber and Zenica generally, did he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had no knowledge of a specific attack or intended attack coming from the Bosnian army prior to being shelled on the morning of the 16th, had you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, no, we hadn't noticed a thing, and we hadn't received any kind of information from anyone that there would be an attack that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were completely surprised when the shelling occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Exactly that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone is Tihomir Blaskic. You knew that at the time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I knew from these conversations, but until then I hadn't met him, or later for that matter, Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, you knew that Mario Cerkez was the commander of the Viteska Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know that he was the commander, but I knew he was something in that brigade, that he had some kind of a position in this chain of command, but, believe me, I didn't know. I was not in touch with the command, and I didn't know what their hierarchy was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then in your particular village, the shelling didn't occur until 9.30, 9.00 or 9.30. I think that's your evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, not after 9.00 but before 9.00, rather, so around 9.00, perhaps 15 minutes before 9.00, but around 9.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between about 5.30 when you said that you first heard shooting coming from the Vitez direction and the direction of Ahmici and Santici and the shelling of the village, that's about three hours, three hours or so, did you hear intense fighting or intense military activity in the area of Ahmici, Santici, and Vitez? Did it increase?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. More intense and more frequent shooting could be heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You received no phone calls from anyone in Ahmici or Santici in relation to the Croats being --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- attacked in those villages? Zoran Kupreskic didn't ring you and say that the village was being attacked by Muslims or the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No, no one called me from a single village, and no one told me that they were attacked or that I would be attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from having a telephone, you also had a radio transmitter in your house, is that correct, or in your garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I don't understand. What kind of a radio transmitter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A radio that you can use to communicate with other villages or Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I did not have a radio transmitter. I did not have a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you have some sort of transmitting device, communication device, other than a telephone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, this was a radio that belonged to Mr. Tomislav Gruban who was one of my deputies, as you call them. He got an old radio transmitter from a friend, a Serb from Tolovici, and he had it. That day, we tried to establish radio communications with that device, but the batteries were poor or something. We did not establish communications with anyone that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was that radio transmitter on your property or was it on his property?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, then at that time, it was empty because I had my car battery in the garage, and then we tried to fill up that battery in my garage, and that is the reason why we had the radio transmitter on my property at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the intention of the radio transmitter? Was it to communicate with other village guards or the central Viteska Brigade in Vitez? What was the purpose of it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: This radio transmitter was used by the mentioned gentlemen to show off, that's the right way of putting it, and it was only on that day that we tried to use it because he said that he had a relative living in the centre of Vitez, and he gave him the right number and whatever, and then we tried to use that radio transmitter, and we tried to reach that relative of his who worked in the communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that at about a quarter to nine, the shelling commenced in Poculica, and I think you said in your evidence that it occurred initially in a sporadic fashion, intermittent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would that be? Would that be one shell every 15 minutes or can you give us an idea of the rate of the shelling in this early period?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, they would fire five or six shells one after another, and then there would be an interval of some 20 minutes or so without any shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this rate of shelling go on for? Did it ever intensify more than that or was that the rate of shelling throughout the day prior to you evacuating?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Twelve hours after we received the ultimatum from the mosque, the shelling became more intense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shelling, did that occur in the part of the village that you lived in, in the purely Croat part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the shelling occurred, you mentioned that someone got in touch with you, I think, and Asim Krehic said to you that he wanted to go to the upper part of the village; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: What is correct is that Asim Krehic's son was the one who came to tell me how terrified he was after he went to the upper part of the village, after having seen all these Mujahedin and troops from the outside. He simply came there to warn me or something, and he did not know the exact answer either when I asked him, "Well, all right, I mean, why did you come and what do you mean?" And he said, "I don't know myself," but I saw that this young man was frightened, and I realised that he wanted to help us, to warn us, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time did you hear the call from the mosque, the speaker from the mosque, for you to surrender? About what time was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: About 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it was only the lower part of the village that you saw that was shelled that morning, the purely Croat part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your role between 9.00 and 12.00? What was your role during that period as the coordinator of the village guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I didn't know what their role was myself -- what my role was. I really couldn't be -- I wasn't actually sure what to do. I tried to visit as many of my neighbours as possible to figure out what to do. I was taking care of my family, tried to make sure that they went to the shelters. So all of that time, we were practically running around the village thinking about what to do because we were taken by surprise. I didn't have any kind of military expert or anybody who could really think of something clever to do that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you keep to the lower part of the village or did you ever move beyond the purely Croat area, namely, beyond Mara Papic's house that morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, until 11.30, I was above the house of Mara Papic at 11.30 for the last time, and, as I pointed out on the map, that was behind the school. I was behind the school at about that time to take care of the wounded person, and then three or four times, I went to that part around the school. Above the school, to the upper part, I didn't go until that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any soldiers yourself on that day, Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't come into the lower part of the village whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the evacuation, did they come into the next part of the village that was 60 per cent Croat and 40 per cent Muslim?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, before the evacuation. That was the reason we decided to evacuate. They captured that part, that was 60 per cent Croatian and 40 per cent Muslim. So my neighbours who were standing around their houses, when they saw how many of them there were and how armed they were, and how they were shouting, they simply withdrew to the lower part of the village. That was the reason we evacuated the civilians, because that part was captured by the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that some of the people in the village told you that the shelling had come from different places. You were told that in the lower part of the village there was shelling from Sljivcica and, in the middle part, shelling from Vrhovine and, in the upper part, there was shelling from Tolovici and Vjetrenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, they had the feeling when they were patrolling. That's how it appeared to us. Some people would say that it was fired from Sljivcica, somebody else would say that it had been from Sljivcica in the upper part. They thought that the shelling came more from Tolovici and Vrhovine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally yourself didn't know where the shelling had come from, apart from what people had told you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, it's true and it's not true. The shelling of my house, as far as that's concerned, I think that came from the direction of Preocica Stijena. So at the time I thought that they were shelling my house from above, but, as I said, everybody had their own opinion, and it's a fact that these mortars were deployed at several points around the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the main reason why you assumed that the shelling had come from those particular areas, is because you had previous knowledge that mortars were deployed prior to the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: We didn't know exactly, but according to the indications and the trenches that were being dug towards Vjetrenica and in Banovac and in the forest close to Vrhovine and then around Tolovici, the trenches that we noticed there, we assumed that the mortars were there. And some heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Sljivcica is in the direction of Vitez, is that correct, closer to Vitez than Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, but that Sljivcica is not a village. It's like a little hill, a meadow, and there are no houses there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far away from Poculica is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Well, that depends where you look at Poculica from. The central part of the village to my house is maybe 500 from the lower part of the villages, two or three hundred metres. As the crow flies from the upper part of the village to Sljivcica, it's maybe 1.000 or 1.500 metres, but if you walk it's about 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A witness has provided some information in relation to where he or she believed that the shelling came from. A witness has stated that on that morning that he or she saw some shelling coming from the Vitez area towards Poculica. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I doubt it. From the direction of Vitez I didn't hear any shells or I couldn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, in relation to that piece of evidence or that question, the basis for it was a witness statement that the Tribunal has. This person's name, I don't think, is necessary that their name be disclosed, and that's why the information wasn't put to the witness. But I would like to tender that document but have it sealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This is a witness who was called in another trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, he or she hasn't been called in another trial, but has provided a statement to the Tribunal in 1995. I am not persisting with this. Just so that the question was substantiated. That's why the information was supplied to the Defence, if there was some problem with that. I am in Your Honours' hands in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, we -- Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, I was going to say we will not admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said there was about 400 or so Croats that lived in the village of Poculica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Most of the Croats were evacuated on the 16th of April. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said about 70 of them that lived in the part of the village towards <obscured> were detained, one group was detained in a community centre and another group was detained in some Muslim houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: It's true that I said that 70 of them were captured that day, mostly from the upper part of the village and the central part. Many more Croats lived in that area and they managed to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You organised the main evacuation about 2.30 in the afternoon, or had people escaped earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: People had escaped earlier into the forest, in the stream. Some of them were in their house shelters, in the cellars, and then we talked about 5.30. Then after that fierce attack from the direction of the mosque, when the people who were standing around their houses had to withdraw below the last Muslim house. Then at about 4.30 we came to the conclusion that we had to evacuate all the civilians. I'm sorry, at 2.30. This then happened at around 3.30. And then after an interval we tried to send everybody from the cellars into the forest where some people already were and then organize withdrawal towards Krizancevo Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that when the evacuation was being carried out in relation to some of the Croat civilians that they were being fired upon as they were leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I said that. They were shooting from the direction of Sljivcica when they were coming down this meadow. You could see that on the videotape. There was a clearing, a meadow, and then they fired at the civilians from Sljivcica with heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it's your evidence that no one was killed as they were being evacuated whilst they were under fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think your evidence is that on the day of the 16th of April there was one person, one Croat killed, and I think you mentioned his name is Anto Kristo. Do you know how he was killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I, after a couple of days when we went over the events, I found out later from the men who remained in that section, in the purely Croatian section, that also while they were withdrawing Anto Kristo was killed. They located the exact position where the sniper shot him in the forehead. They assumed that the sniper was in a house of one of the Muslim neighbours, and the house was in the central part of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any Muslims being killed on that day as well in the village? Redzo Bektas, was he killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I found that out only after the war, maybe a year back when I met one of my neighbours, a Muslim. So we talked about everything that had happened. He told me then that on the first day one person, I think he said his name was Redzo, was killed. If that's the person that I am thinking of, I knew this man, he was from Prnjavor. So maybe about a year ago I found out that on the first day in Poculica a Muslim soldier was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know some people in detention, you stated that they were killed about a week after the attack on Poculica. You said three people were killed in -- is it the community centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that have been about the 25th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: No. Maybe the 22nd or the 23rd of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were no people that were in detention on the 16th of April that were killed, either the women or children or the men? I think you stated that the women and the children, or the people that were taken to the Muslim houses, were treated quite well, some of the locals were quite embarrassed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: The people who were killed at the hall, three men, three Croat men, were captured on the 16th of April in the village of Poculica. Among the women who were wounded were women from Putkovici, who were also brought to this hall. And then the children, I don't know if they were inside at that time. I think that they weren't. I said that usually women with small children were placed in the houses of Muslims where they were brought and left. So in most cases they were satisfied with the attitude of the hosts towards them at that time, as much as that was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated in your evidence that some of the men kept at the community centre were sent out to dig some trenches?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. When they came from captivity, I heard that from them, from the people who were captured. And they told us these stories about digging trenches, about burying the cattle in the village. All the pigs in the village were slaughtered, the Mujahedins had slaughtered all the pigs that remained in the village. Then they made our captives bury them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This activity of trench-digging, are you aware that that was an activity that was carried out by the HVO as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the same thing from the stories. I didn't see it personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you left the village of Poculica, I think you were wounded and then you were evacuated by some other people that assisted you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have time, I would assume, to examine what damage occurred on the 16th of April in the Poculica village as a whole, damage to Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: That evening there was no time. Naturally, nobody thought about the material consequences. The only thing we worried about was who was alive. We took hours to evacuate. This wasn't organised, so we left at about 3.30, and then there were men who came in the evening, or in the morning, to Krizancevo Selo. And there was no communication. The lower part of the village didn't know what was happening in the upper part. When they saw that there was nobody there, they withdrew slowly and then they arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you stated in your evidence that your house was burnt, completely burnt about a week after the attack.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I think about a week later. That's when it started, maybe the 3rd or 4th day, because our men who had pulled out and had come to Krizancevo Selo, they were on the lines above Krizancevo Selo. And then from that part, which was towards Tolovici, you could see the village of Poculica very well. So every day they would watch one or two houses being torched. Before that, I think, that my house I could watch from Vitez. I had gone to visit my sister after being bandaged, so I could see with binoculars how the tractor in front of my house was being loaded with the heating radiators from the ground floor. Then I could see a young man carrying the sun umbrella. He had opened it and he was coming out of my yard onto the street and waving it around. After 45 minutes I could see smoke from my bedroom. You could see the smoke from there first. Also, my brother's house was torched the next day after mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the case, isn't it, that a large number of these houses were damaged and destroyed for the ones you've mentioned sometime after the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Ninety-nine per cent or 100 per cent of them were burnt. There was some minor damage from the shelling on that day, but later they were torched; plundered and burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you mentioned that some of the men that were detained were released, I think, about the 16th of May, '93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them were released earlier, but at that time I was wounded and I had personal problems. I was receiving treatment at the health clinic. But I think on the 15th of May a larger exchange was organised, and I think that the majority of Croats from Poculica were exchanged at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO were handing over the prisoners that they had in exchange for the prisoners that the Bosnian army had. Is that how you understand it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, I think this was done in that way through the Red Cross and all of these organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can just have a moment, Your Honour. I think I am nearly finished my questioning. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Smith. We have 10 minutes. I wonder, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, do you think you could start now and finish as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Probably I will not be able to finish, Mr. President. I can start or maybe we can leave this for tomorrow, if that is all right with Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, no, let's start.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, I seek to tender those documents, subject to the one that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 345 and document 346.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No objection from the Defence? I don't see any objection. They are admitted into the evidence. Re-examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Grebenar, in relation to the victims, the persons who were killed in the hall in Prnjavor, you mentioned this and you were asked whether these were people from Poculica. Could you give us the names of the persons who were killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, Pero Papic, the son of Pero, born in 1960. I know this information because I went to school with him. Jozo Vidovic, I think he was maybe born in about 1947. Also, Ivo Vidovic, I think he was born in 1945 or '43, somewhere around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the people who were wounded on that occasion? You said that there were five women in question who were from Putkovici, and out of the nine wounded persons, do you know any of their names or rather, were some of them from Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I know two names, and I think they were seriously wounded. They were from Poculica. Zeljo Papic, son of Milko, I think he was born in 1965. And Jozo Jucic, son of Ilija, I think he was born in 1942 or '43. They were gravely wounded, particularly, Zeljo Papic, and then I really don't know the names of the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Jozo Jurcevic, was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, Jozo Jurcevic, son of Ilija, was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what year he was born in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: 1941 or 1942 perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anto Anic and Pero Papic, do those names ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Pero Papic is the person who was killed. There's also his father, Pero Papic, I think he was wounded. Anto Anic is not a familiar name. Perhaps that's someone from another village. I don't know him. He's not from Poculica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Milko Papic, was he from Poculica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. Milko Papic was the father of Zeljo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I think he was there -- he was wounded, but I don't know how serious it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in relation to what you said to the Prosecutor in response to his questions, when you talked about your withdrawal from Poculica, you talked about evacuation. Do you think that you were evacuated then or do you think that you were expelled? What do you think about that? Do you know what the distinction would be between the two?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: When I talked about evacuation, I talked about the rescue of people, and my opinion is that evacuation is carried out when a person is faced with danger from a natural disaster or, in this case, it was from the fact that the Muslim army forced us to expulsion. That's a better word than "evacuation." We had to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the houses, when you talked about 40 Croat houses that were burned, you said that the other houses that were not destroyed were used by Muslims, that people moved into them, and that there was no destruction of those houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, there was no destruction. They weren't completely devastated, but they weren't being maintained, so that those houses now, five years after use by them, are not in the condition that they should have been if their hosts had been living there and maintaining them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those houses being used until the present day by Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: All the livable houses of Croats in the village of Poculica, meaning the local community of Poculica, are in the possession of Muslims and occupied by Muslims, so all of those houses that are in livable condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said as far as Poculica itself is concerned, that Croats did not return to that area. Did they return to the surrounding villages that were populated by Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: As far as I know, a small number returned around Buhine Kuce, and there was some renovation there. A little bit was done in Krtina Mahala, but I don't have any information whether anybody returned there. Then in the rest of the municipality, there has been no significant change or progress as far as the return of expelled Croats is concerned or the repair of Croat homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any Croats returning to Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: I heard something, that there was a project being carried out there, a return project, and there was agreement between the parties, the HDZ and the SDA, of return to Grbavica in exchange for the return of certain Croats in those border areas. I know that for Grbavica, it was implemented 100 per cent, but I really don't know how many Croats returned to Kruscica. I don't have exact information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the village of Bobasi?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes. This was all part of that concept, the village of Bobasi, Kruscica, and the so-called Barisi Kuce, and then on the other side, it should have been Grbavica. Some work was done, some repair work, but I don't think that that's at any kind of stage of completion. The level of their completion really is not such that it's possible for people to move in. I think some people did return, but it's a very small number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said before the conflict, that is to say, before the 16th of April, 1993, that the number of persons, Croats, involved in the village guards was 40; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Yes, that's about the number. I don't have the exact number written down, but I think, yes, that's the figure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many members from the Muslim side there were in the village guards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: At that time, they had a much larger number, but the number of persons who were on guard in this part of the village, compared to Vrhovine and Prnjavor, was much smaller. So in Poculica, maybe there were about 50 of them, maybe more. We would meet, and we also sometimes had watches together, but there was much more of them than us in Poculica. And then in the villages of Prnjavor and Vrhovine, they had a lot of refugees and a lot of outsiders, so the MOS was formed by some Mujahedin, so there were some units there. And then in the evening from the mosque, we could hear the music, and you could never hear this in Poculica before, not particularly so loud so that the whole village could hear it. There were many more of them in the village guards on that side than on our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned in your statement, and partly you repeated this during the cross-examination, that at first, Croat guards were separate, and then that Muslim guards were set up. Tell me, during which period of time did you have joint guard duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN GREBENAR (Cont'd)
utterances.text: Perhaps in the second half of '92. Maybe one to two months we were together until what I just talked about occurred, where you would see these very young men who didn't even shave, they were acting as Mujahedin, and they started to grow beards. That's how they started to turn up for the guard duty. So in that period, we had these joint watches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I see that you can't complete today, so we will adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
